title: MarkdStage — Windows, Node.js, and GitHub Copilot App
description: Create Markdown slides, edit diagrams, present, and export PDF or PowerPoint. Find installation instructions and workflows for Windows, Node.js, and GitHub Copilot App.
heroDescription: MarkdStage uses Markdown as the source for slides. Edit diagrams, review layouts, present, and export PDF or PowerPoint in the Windows app, the Node.js CLI, or GitHub Copilot App. Choose your environment for installation instructions and workflows.
heroAlt: A MarkdStage slide showing an architecture diagram connecting a browser, API, and database.
heroCaption: Rendered slide defined with Architecture DSL
heroNote: All three environments use the same Markdown format. Ask AI to create or revise the source, or edit it directly in a text editor.

needs.title: Separate content from appearance
needs.body: Edit text in Markdown and adjust colors and typography through themes. Keep the theme while revising the content.

needs.title: Make small changes directly
needs.body: Edit wording in an external text editor. Adjust Architecture diagram positions and properties in the visual editor, then select Save to update Markdown.

needs.title: Check fit and appearance
needs.body: Use Output preview to check fixed 16:9 slides. CLI commands and Canvas operations also provide layout diagnostics and selected-page images for review.

examplesDescription: Switch between examples to view the rendered slides and their Markdown source. You can also download the example Markdown files.
markdownAlt: A dark slide with a heading, three bullet points, and syntax-highlighted JavaScript.
architectureAlt: An architecture diagram connecting a browser, API, and database, with positions, icons, and connectors defined in Architecture DSL.
markdownDescription: Write text, bullet lists, and code blocks in Markdown, with syntax highlighting for code. Use Mermaid for automatic, relationship-driven diagram layout; its colors can also follow the theme.
architectureDescription: Create architecture diagrams with JSON-based Architecture DSL inside Markdown. Specify positions, sizes, groups, icons, and connectors when you want to compose a diagram for the slide.
editorDescription: On a slide containing an Architecture diagram, choose More controls > Shape editing to open Architecture Editor. Adjust positions or properties, then select Save to update Markdown. Moving a shape alone does not save the change.
editorAlt: The native Windows Architecture Editor with the sample API node selected and its position and properties displayed.
editorCaption: Edit the diagram in Windows Architecture Editor, then select Save.

steps.title: Prepare the Markdown source
steps.body: Download an example or write Markdown in a text editor. To ask AI for a draft, provide source material, an audience, and a presentation length. The platform tabs below explain the available AI workflows.
steps.detail: Sample or text editor · Optional AI · Theme

steps.title: Refine directly and inspect
steps.body: Open the Markdown in your chosen environment and review each slide. Revise text in the source and adjust Architecture diagrams on screen. After changes, check the fixed 16:9 output preview.
steps.detail: Text editing · Diagram placement · Layout diagnostics

steps.title: Present and share
steps.body: Keep speaker notes in front of you while displaying slides on another screen. Review every page of the final output before sharing a PDF or PowerPoint file to suit the recipient's needs.

shareDescription: Export PDF and PowerPoint from Windows, Node.js, or GitHub Copilot App. Choose a format for the next task and review the file before sharing. Each platform tab explains its export controls and output paths.
pdfDescription: Export fixed 16:9 slides for a PDF viewer. Speaker notes are not included.
pptxDescription: Supported text, tables, code, and Architecture diagrams remain editable; unsupported representations use images. Speaker notes are included. PowerPoint edits do not round-trip to Markdown, and output is not guaranteed to be pixel-identical.
startDescription: Choose an environment to see its installation, authoring, presentation, export, and examples. You do not need to install all three.
cliDescription: Install the CLI from npm and use the browser to review slides and edit diagrams. Present and export through the UI or commands. Optionally install a Skill to work through Claude Code or Codex. GitHub Copilot App is not required.
cliRequirements: The npm distribution requires Node.js 24 or later and installed Edge, Chrome, or Chromium.
cliInstallDescription: Run this command in a terminal to install the CLI. Run the remaining commands from the folder where you keep the deck.
cliResolutionNote: If the Store package is also installed, replace markdstage at the start of a command with npx @markdstage/markdstage to explicitly run the npm distribution.
cliSkillTitle: Optional AI setup: install a workspace Skill
cliSkillDescription: In the deck folder, register the Skill for your AI tool. This example uses Claude Code. Skip Skill installation if you do not use AI.
cliAlternative: For Codex, replace the Skill registration line with the following. You do not need both.
cliAuthorDescription: Download a sample or create slides.md in a text editor. To use AI, open the folder containing the installed Skill in Claude Code or Codex and provide source material or notes with a request like this. You do not need an existing slides.md.
authorPrompt: Use the markdstage skill to create five slides for a technical audience from these notes in slides.md. Use the dark theme, preview the deck, and check the layout.
refinePrompt: Keep the theme and shorten only the explanation on slide 2.
cliPreviewDescription: Use this command to open the browser. Saving Markdown in an external editor refreshes the display. Edit Architecture diagrams through More controls > Shape editing and select Save to update the source Markdown. Moving a shape alone does not save it.
cliSessionNote: Keep this terminal running while you preview. Run diagnostics or exports in another terminal opened to the same working folder. Press Ctrl+C to stop the preview.
cliInspectDescription: Ask the same AI to check fit. It follows the Skill's diagnostic workflow, so you do not need to name the commands.
inspectPrompt: Check whether the content fits on the slides. Identify any clipping and review images of the pages that need a closer look.
cliCheckDescription: Run these commands yourself or through an AI tool. validate checks structure, themes, and DSL; inspect checks fixed 16:9 clipping. capture --pages produces images of selected pages for visual review.
cliDeliveryDescription: These commands use --output to set the destination. Exports from More controls in the browser are saved beside the source Markdown with the same filename stem, replacing existing output with that name. Copy previous output first or use the CLI to choose a different name. PPTX contains editable text and shapes as well as content exported as images. PowerPoint changes do not update Markdown.
cliNext: In the browser's presenter view, select Start presentation to open the audience window. Speaker notes appear only in the presenter view. Press Ctrl+C in the terminal when you want to stop the local server.
desktopDescription: Manage workspace files, install Agent Skills, edit Architecture diagrams, check output layout, present with notes, and export PDF or PowerPoint from the GUI. The included CLI supports agent and terminal workflows. GitHub Copilot App is not required.
desktopDetail: Windows 10 version 1809 or later, x64 or ARM64. Native UI and validation use WebView2; inspection, capture, and GUI/CLI export also need installed Edge, Chrome, or Chromium. Node.js is not required. Portable ZIPs and checksums are available from Releases; ZIPs do not register the CLI alias.
windowsAuthorDescription: Download a sample or create slides.md in a text editor, then open it from the workspace file list. For AI-assisted creation, open the folder containing the installed Skill in your external AI tool. The Windows app has no built-in AI chat.
windowsReview: Check that More controls > Output preview is enabled; it is on by default. Review clipping warnings and adjust text or diagrams when needed. The included CLI also provides validate, inspect, and capture commands.
windowsPresent: Choose More controls > Presenter view to see the current and next slides and speaker notes. Select Start presentation to open the audience window and move it to the presentation display. The audience sees the slides without notes.
windowsExport: Choose More controls > Export PDF or Export PowerPoint. Output is saved beside the source Markdown with the same filename stem. Existing output with that name is replaced. For another filename, use --output in the included CLI.

windowsSteps.title: Install from Microsoft Store
windowsSteps.body: Install MarkdStage, then open the application. The package also adds the markdstage CLI alias. If the command is unavailable, open a new terminal and check Windows App execution aliases.

windowsSteps.title: Open a workspace
windowsSteps.body: Choose Open folder… and select the folder containing your Markdown files. Open a file from MARKDOWN FILES. Save text changes in your external editor; Desktop watches the source.

windowsSteps.title: Install workspace Skills when needed
windowsSteps.body: Select Install skills… and choose Codex, Claude Code, or GitHub Copilot. Open the same folder in that AI tool. Skills do not install the agent or Canvas Extension; modified files are preserved unless you explicitly force replacement.

workspaceAlt: Windows workspace with slides.md in the file list and the Install skills command.
workspaceCaption: Choose a folder and open its Markdown file.
skillsAlt: Windows dialog with Codex, Claude Code, and GitHub Copilot Skill targets and an unchecked force-overwrite option.
skillsCaption: Install only the workspace Skill targets you use.
windowsWorkflowDescription: Follow a web service architecture presentation from creation through presenting and export. See how to ask an AI agent for the slides, adjust the diagram on screen, and edit text and shapes in PowerPoint.
recordingNote: Choose English or Japanese captions. Manage slide text, diagrams, and speaker notes in Markdown files; use PDF for sharing and PPTX for further editing in PowerPoint. The PowerPoint interface is Japanese. Edits there do not update the original Markdown file.
recordingSteps: 0:00–0:18 — Ask an AI agent for six slides explaining a web service architecture. Include a diagram and speaker notes, and ask it to fix errors or text that extends beyond the slides.
0:18–0:32 — Prepare a Markdown file containing slide text, diagrams, and speaker notes. The six slides plus an automatic back cover make seven pages.
0:32–0:50 — Open slides.md in MarkdStage and use the slide list to choose the diagram page.
0:50–1:18 — Edit the diagram on screen. Drag the API node and save; the change is reflected in both the Markdown source file and the displayed slide.
1:18–1:43 — Present with the current and next slides and speaker notes. The audience window shows only the slides, without the notes.
1:43–2:23 — Export PDF for reading and sharing, or PPTX for further editing in PowerPoint. Files are saved beside the Markdown source. Speaker notes are not included in the PDF.
2:23–2:54 — Change the heading text and API shape color in PowerPoint, then save. Editing in PowerPoint does not change the original Markdown file.
2:54–3:04 — Keep the Markdown source and choose PDF or PPTX for the next task. Some PPTX content is exported as images rather than editable text or shapes.
nodeExampleDescription: Try a deck with an architecture diagram and speaker notes in the browser. Save the downloaded Markdown as slides.md in your working folder.
nodeExampleSteps: Open slides.md with the preview command above, then choose the architecture diagram from the slide list.
Choose More controls > Shape editing, move the API node, and select Save. The source Markdown and displayed slide reflect the change.
Run the diagnostic commands to check structure and fit, and revise the Markdown as needed.
Use present to open presenter view, or export to write PDF or PPTX.
nodePreviewAlt: The Node.js browser UI displaying the architecture diagram from the service example.
nodePreviewCaption: Browser UI opened by the Node.js preview command.
canvasDescription: Display slides in the GitHub Copilot App canvas. Ask Copilot to create Markdown or revise diagrams, or open Markdown files directly to display them.
canvasRequirements: Requires GitHub Copilot App with permission to install Canvas Extensions. You do not need the Windows or npm distribution of MarkdStage. Export uses installed Edge, Chrome, or Chromium.
canvasInstructions: Ask GitHub Copilot App to install the Canvas Extension at user scope:
canvasPrompt: Install MarkdStage at user scope from the following GitHub repository folder.
canvasWarning: The Extension runs local code. Review its contents before installing and use a trusted release.
canvasNext: Open the workspace containing your materials in GitHub Copilot App and ask for a deck from your notes or source documents. Copilot can write Markdown and display it in MarkdStage Canvas alongside the same conversation.
canvasAuthorPrompt: Create five slides for a technical audience from these notes. Save them as slides.md with the dark theme and display them in MarkdStage Canvas.
canvasReview: Ask Copilot to check whether the content fits on the slides. Copilot uses inspect_layout and images of selected pages. For manual review, ensure More controls > Output preview is enabled; do not toggle it off if already checked.
canvasEdit: Ask Copilot to revise text or diagrams, or open More controls > Shape editing on an Architecture diagram to adjust it on screen. Select Save in the visual editor to write the changes to the source Markdown.
canvasDirect: To open a file without AI, choose More controls > Open Markdown. Select Refresh automatically on save to reflect changes saved in an external editor.
canvasPresent: Choose More controls > Presenter view for the current and next slides and speaker notes. Select Start presentation to open the audience window and move it to another display. From normal slide view, More controls > External window also opens it. Canvas and the audience window stay on the same page.
canvasExport: With a Markdown file open, More controls > Export PDF / Export PowerPoint saves beside the source with the same filename stem, replacing existing output with that name. Copy previous output first or ask Copilot to export to a different path. PPTX contains editable text and shapes as well as image fallbacks. PowerPoint edits do not update the source Markdown.
canvasExportPrompt: Export this deck as slides.pdf and slides.pptx. Tell me where the files were saved so I can review the output.
canvasExampleDescription: Save the same service architecture sample as slides.md in the workspace, then try these requests in order. The hands-on guide also covers creating a new deck.
canvasOpenPrompt: Open slides.md in MarkdStage Canvas and refresh the display whenever I save the source file.
canvasRefinePrompt: Move the API node in the architecture diagram slightly to the right. Save the change to slides.md and check that the whole diagram fits on the slide.
canvasExampleCaption: Shared Architecture DSL output example. Copilot requests also keep the diagram in the source Markdown.
macNote: is available as a separate project. It is developed, released, and supported outside this repository.
copyFailed: Could not copy. Select the text and copy it manually.
copyUnavailable: Clipboard is unavailable. Select the text and copy it manually.
